topic: Ten Red Flags Before Buying a Commercial Property
caption:
Before you sign a commercial purchase agreement, a promising price can hide expensive problems. Lesson 34 walks through core diligence areas—physical condition, income verification, legal/zoning status, environmental exposure, and operational risks—and gives concrete steps you can use immediately. Document each red flag with photos, inspection reports, and written tenant confirmations. Use those documents to negotiate price reductions, escrowed repair caps, or required remediation timelines. For industrial sites order a Phase I environmental; for older buildings get structural and MEP inspections. Always verify rent rolls against bank statements and confirm tenant identities before assuming income. If you're active in Chester or Montgomery Counties, add local checks: meet the township zoning officer, confirm sewer and traffic constraints, and ask neighboring landlords about demand and turnover. Want a one-page printable checklist tailored to these counties or a short review of a deal? Get the checklist and resources at dmsellscre.com/investors or DM me your basic property details to start.
